messages:
jane_acme: Hey team — I accepted the org invite for Acme Corp and I can see org settings & billing, but whenever I try to open project 'alpha' I get a 403 Permission denied. My account is in the Azure AD group that should map to Org Admins. Can someone confirm what I should check?

maria_support: sorry you're blocked — can you paste the exact error body or a screenshot? also: was the invite via SSO (enterprise SAML/Azure) or an email link?

jane_acme: SSO via Azure AD. Accepted by clicking the email link from the invite. Screenshot: https://acme.screenshots/ok (redacted) — response shows: 403 Forbidden, message: \"You do not have access to this project\".

deploy-bot: SCIM sync job finished for acme-corp at 2026-03-15T12:45:23Z — groups: 2 updated, users: 1 added, duration: 6.2s

kevin_iam: @maria_support @jane_acme quick checklist: 1) Are you visible in the org's members list in the console? 2) Is your account assigned to the Azure enterprise app mapping that pushes SCIM groups? 3) Can you share a curl reproduce (no creds) showing x-request-id / headers so we can find the request in logs?

jane_acme: I am listed under Org -> Members as \"Org Admin\" in Azure but in Console I see my user as member (not admin). I ran a quick curl to test (I replaced token):

```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer ey...REDACTED...\" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/projects/alpha
* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.10.10.10) port 443 (#0)\n> GET /v1/projects/alpha HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.example\n> Authorization: Bearer ey...\n< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\n< x-redwood-error: forbidden.project_access\n< x-request-id: 01H7Z9A2B3C4D5\n< content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8\n{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": \"forbidden.project_access\",\n    \"message\": \"You do not have access to this project\"\n  }\n}\n```

jordan_cs: thanks — that x-request-id is perfect. I'll pull logs. preliminary thought: SCIM group->role mapping at org level didn't include the group name that Azure emitted. often causes: group renames, or claims not including the expected object id.

kevin_iam: two fast paths: 1) short-term workaround — we can add you directly to the project as project_admin via the Admin API or console, that'll unblock you immediately. 2) longer-term fix — fix the SCIM/claims mapping so the Azure group maps to the OrgAdmin role and re-run a sync. Which do you prefer?

maria_support: @jane_acme if you want to try workaround 1, send your email or user id and I can add you. if you'd prefer org fix, we'll need your IdP admin to check the enterprise app group/claim config (groups claim, or app roles).

jane_acme: please do the quick add for now, email is jane@acme.example. I'd like to understand the root cause too.

maria_support: on it, adding now...

deploy-bot: Admin action: added role project_admin to user jane@acme.example on project alpha by maria_support at 2026-03-15T12:58:03Z (audit-id: AUD-3382)

jane_acme: tried again — I can open the project now, can access settings and create resources. thanks! :relieved:

kevin_iam: great. root cause notes for the ticket: found SCIM sync logs for acme-corp — Azure emitted the group's displayName as \"Acme Admins v2\" but our SCIM mapping rule expected exact match \"acme-org-admins\". the provisioning job therefore skipped mapping that group to the OrgAdmin role. we also saw a group claim mismatch in the SAML assertion earlier (no appRole claim).

```
# snippet from SCIM provisioning log
2026-03-15T12:45:23Z INFO provisioning: processing group Acme Admins v2 (id: 0a1b2c3d)
2026-03-15T12:45:23Z WARN mapping: group name not matched -> skipping role assignment
```

kevin_iam: actions taken: updated SCIM group pattern to allow case-insensitive / partial matches (to handle suffixes like \"v2\"), forced an immediate provision sync via the internal API, and opened an internal ticket to make group matching more robust. run we executed:

```
POST https://console.redwood.internal/internal/scim/provision/sync?force=true
# returned 200, re-applied roles to 1 user
```

jordan_cs: recommended IdP guidance (share with Acme AD admin): make sure the enterprise app sends groups in the SAML/OSO token or exposes them via SCIM with stable identifiers (objectId). avoid relying solely on displayName; prefer group id mapping or a custom claim like `redwood_role`. sample guidance: set group claim to \"SecurityGroups\" and include group objectId for deterministic mapping.

maria_support: I'll follow up with the customer with: 1) what we changed on our side, 2) recommended IdP config, and 3) note that we added them directly to the project as a temporary fix.

jane_acme: appreciated — if you can include the exact steps to avoid this in the future that'd be great (our IT team will update).

kevin_iam: will put the short how-to in the ticket: prefer: SCIM groups with stable IDs (objectId), or add a custom claim `redwood_role: org_admin` for the enterprise app. also recommend running a manual Provision sync after making mapping changes.

maria_support: closing this thread since access is restored — reopening if anything else pops up. tag: INC-7890 for the IAM follow-up. :white_check_mark: 

jane_acme: thanks all, huge help!
